newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swissair staff in France plans strikes.
newsitem.headline: Swissair staff in France plans strikes.

text.p: Swissair AG said its staff in France was planning further strike action today in response to the carrier's plans to cut jobs and reduce salaries.
A Swissair spokesman said there might be some minor delays to flights between Switzerland and France, but overall the carrier expects connections to be normal.
Swissair's cargo operations between the two countries, however, will be severely curtailed.
The spokesman said the carrier had stopped shipping cargo between France and Switzerland as there is no handling in Paris.

On Wednesday large parts of Swissair's staff in France of some 250 people went on strike after Swissair said it planned to cut 66 jobs, but also create 30 new jobs as part of a restructuring of its operations there.

The measures include partial outsourcing of Swissair's cargo activities at Charles de Gaulle airport near Paris from January 1, 1997 and closing five offices in the cities of Grenoble, Marseille, Nantes, Toulouse and Strassbourg from March 1.
